methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Daylight Computer is a Series A-stage consumer technology company that has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis operates without access to a comparable company universe; no public peers were identified, and private comps were unavailable for triangulation.

The stage-progression method provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a proxy for enterprise value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $20M. This reflects the standard risk-adjusted return expectation between early institutional rounds and later venture stages, absent company-specific operating metrics or revenue data to support alternative approaches.

The analysis triangulates to a median valuation of $20M, with a supported range of $17M to $23M. The range reflects residual uncertainty inherent in stage-based multiples when applied without operating leverage, revenue trajectory, or comparable exit benchmarks. Key uncertainties include: (1) absence of publicly-traded consumer tech comparables to validate stage-appropriate multiples; (2) lack of private peer transactions in the comp set; and (3) no disclosed revenue, unit economics, or growth metrics to anchor a revenue or earnings-based valuation. The $20M median should be treated as a stage-calibrated estimate rather than a market-substantiated valuation. Any material revision would require disclosure of operational milestones or identification of relevant trading comparables.
